newsitem.title: USA: Dividend, buyback hike eyed at RJR Nabisco.
newsitem.headline: Dividend, buyback hike eyed at RJR Nabisco.

text.p: RJR Nabisco Holdings Corp, embattled with shareholders who feel the stock is undervalued, may announce plans to return value to stockholders Wednesday through a higher dividend and stepped-up share-repurchase plan, one analyst said.

Smith Barney analyst Martin Feldman said he expects the company, during its presentation Wednesday at a consumer products conference, will announce it is raising its dividend to $2.05 to $2.10 per share annually, up from the current payout of $1.85.
Feldman said he expects the company to also announce it will implement a share-repurchase plan for $200 million to $250 million worth of common stock.
RJR Nabisco spokewoman Carol Mackovich said the company's policy is not to comment on market speculation.
RJR Nabisco has drawn the ire of shareholders over the past few years for its reluctance to take steps some shareholders feel is necessary to unlock the depressed value in the stock.

The most ardent of those shareholders, financier and former TWA chief executive Carl Icahn, and Brooke Group Ltd chairman Bennett LeBow, have targeted a spinoff of Nabisco Holdings Corp, which is 80.5-percent owned by RJR Nabisco, as the most promising way to achieve a higher stock price.

The company has said it does not feel the time is right for a spinoff and said it would seek other ways of returning shareholder value. Increased dividends and share repurchases are a standard alternative.

"Their dividend annualizes in April," said Ron Morrow, analyst at Rodman & Renshaw. "They're making a presentation tomorrow. It could be about the right time to announce a dividend increase. It's about time for them to announce (a repurchase) too."
